$comment: EVERY customizable knob of the daily digest lives in this file.
Edit this, commit it, and the next run picks it up. The automation prompt
never needs to change.
If AGENTS.md and this file disagree, this file wins.

automation.name: daily-interest-digest
automation.$comment: id is written by tools/install-automation.ps1. It points at a machine-local Orca project; re-run that script if orca reports the automation as orphaned.

agent.$comment: Switch to codex, claude, gemini, grok, pi, omp... The model is chosen inside the agent, not here.

$comment: indexFile MUST stay tracked by git. The automation checks out a fresh worktree
per run, so an ignored ledger means every run starts with an empty blocklist and
the digest repeats yesterday. That is the one rule. Hence it lives in /ledger/,
NOT inside the gitignored /output/.
outputDir holds generated artifacts (daily .md, PDFs, cards) and is gitignored.
exampleDir is the tracked QA fixture - re-read it after changing style/format.
The standard repo signals worth reporting on any GitHub item. Stars alone tell
you popularity, not whether the thing is usable. Each entry says what to fetch
and when it matters. Trim or extend freely - this is config.

how.stars: Search API returns it. Round it - 823 not 823.4.
how.language: Primary language from the search result.
how.license: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/license or the repo object's license.spdx_id. No license is a real finding: 'no license' means you cannot legally use it. Say that plainly.
how.lastCommit: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} -> pushed_at. Under 30 days is alive; over a year is a corpse with stars.
how.releases: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases.atom - free, no REST quota. No releases on a CLI or library is a maturity signal.
how.contributing: Does CONTRIBUTING.md exist? GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/CONTRIBUTING.md - one cheap call.
how.goodFirstIssue: GET /search/issues?q=repo:{owner}/{repo}+label:"good first issue". Signals the project is recruiting, which matters if you want to fix something rather than just use it.
how.funding: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} -> has_downloads / FUNDING.yml. Sponsored projects have their own incentives; worth knowing before trusting advice.
how.archived: archived:true on the repo object. Read-only, unmaintained - say so.
how.install: The real install command, copied from the README. Never invent one.
how.platform: Windows-native, or Linux/macOS only. Stated, not implied - this machine is Windows.

$comment2: Budget: the unauthenticated REST API allows ~60 requests/hour, 10/min for search.
A 60-item run cannot afford one API call per repo per fact. Cheapest order:
search result already gives stars + language + pushed_at + open_issues + license.
Spend the rest on releases.atom (free) and only check CONTRIBUTING.md or
good-first-issue on Tier A items, where the detail is actually worth the call.

audience.$comment: The 'Use it for' line on every item is written for exactly this person.
audience.runs: Orca worktrees with opencode, codex and agy
audience.$comment2: host matters: say plainly whether a tool is Windows-safe instead of leaving it implied.

$comment: Voice lives in styles/<tone>.md. Change `tone` to switch it - the automation
prompt never changes. Available: punchy (default), analyst, plain, social.
$comment2: How many items in a run get the full in-depth write-up.
Deliberately NOT labelled or ordered as a 'top N'. Nothing here is ranked -
an in-depth item is just the one that needed more explaining. The rest are compact.

$comment: An explicit 'go and look at this' nudge. Deliberately scarce: at most one per
category, and not on the in-depth items (those already carry the hook).
Used too often it reads as a mark-up job and gets skipped.

avoid: at the end of the day
style.$comment3: Banned on sight. Most of these are the fingerprints of generated prose.

$comment: Local files for MANUAL posting. The automation never publishes anywhere -
no dev.to, no API, no keys. It renders a PDF and a set of PNG cards; you copy
whatever you want onto whatever you post to.
HTML -> PDF/PNG via a headless Chromium found at run time (Edge, Chrome).
No pandoc, no wkhtmltopdf, no flameshot, no ImageMagick required.
tools/render_assets.py is stdlib-only Python 3.

categories.name: GitHub projects
categories.focus: New repos in the agent ecosystem showing early traction.
categories.note: Prefer <60 days old. Report the repo facts listed in digest.repoFacts - stars alone is not the signal.

categories.name: CLI tools
categories.focus: Terminal tools that sharpen an agent's loop.
categories.note: Report install method (brew/scoop/npm/cargo/go/pip/uv) and whether it is Windows-safe.

categories.name: MCP servers
categories.focus: Servers that add real capability to Orca/opencode/codex.
categories.note: Report transport (stdio/http) and one example tool call.

categories.name: Agent frameworks & orchestration
categories.focus: Harnesses, multi-agent orchestration, task DAGs, handoffs, eval harnesses, agent memory, context engineering, MCP gateways, sandboxes.
categories.note: The category that matters most. Read closer, write richer notes.

categories.name: Papers & writing worth reading
categories.focus: Real technique, real benchmarks, post-mortems, architecture write-ups, eval methodology. No SEO filler, no '10 best X' listicles.
categories.note: Report reading time and one sentence on why it is worth the time.
